articles.body: TL;DR Android Auto version 18.0 beta includes code suggesting it may support dual-SIM status bar icons. articles.body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google is delaying the rollout of Gemini skills for Workspace users. It says the rollout is on hold to ensure “safe and reliable” access for every enterprise user. Google hasn’t specified a rollout date, but says it will share an update when it is confirmed. Last month, Google confirmed its plans to sunset Gemini’s usage-specific Gems and replace them with skills. These skills are easier to set up, access, and invoke in any conversation , and they don’t force you to use them in an isolated environment like Gems did. With its announcement, Google has already started bringing skills to Gmail users , including those on Gemini’s free tiers. For enterprise users, however, Google set a later rollout date, and it has now been pushed back.

articles.title: A good application doesn't start with code
articles.excerpt: Introduction When you're a developer, it's natural to start a project with the technology. Which stack? Which architecture? Which database? Which API? These are important questions. But they often com…
articles.body: Introduction When you're a developer, it's natural to start a project with the technology. Which stack? Which architecture? Which database? Which API? These are important questions. But they often come too early. Before thinking about code, you need to understand what you're trying to build, for whom, and why . An application can be technically excellent yet solve the wrong problem. Conversely, a simple solution can have enormous value when it precisely meets a real need. A good application starts with a problem to understand, not with code to write. 01 — Start with the problem Before drawing a screen or creating a database, one question must be clear: What problem are we trying to solve? A user generally doesn't think in features.
articles.author: ArmelDev

articles.title: A simple application for the user can be complex behind
articles.excerpt: Introduction — Visible simplicity often hides great complexity When an application is well designed, its use often seems obvious. The user clicks, provides some information and gets a result. They don…
articles.body: Introduction — Visible simplicity often hides great complexity When an application is well designed, its use often seems obvious. The user clicks, provides some information and gets a result. They don’t need to understand what happens behind the scenes. Yet, this apparent simplicity can hide a large amount of logic, rules, and technical decisions. User-side simplicity is often the result of well‑managed system-side complexity. 1. What the user sees The user generally sees only a small part of the application. They see an interface, some buttons, forms, and results. They simply expect to be able to accomplish their goal without having to think about the system’s internal workings. For example, to find a professional, they can simply describe their problem and submit a request.
articles.author: ArmelDev

articles.title: Client-Side PDF Tools in JavaScript: Merge, Compress and Convert Without Uploading tags: javascript, webdev, pdf, privacy
articles.excerpt: Most "free online PDF tools" work the same way: you upload a contract, a bank statement or a scan of your passport, a server does something to it, and you download the result. That's a lot of trust fo…
articles.body: Most "free online PDF tools" work the same way: you upload a contract, a bank statement or a scan of your passport, a server does something to it, and you download the result. That's a lot of trust for merging two files. We recently built a set of 18 free PDF tools that do the opposite: the file is read, changed and saved on your device, and its contents never reach a server. The browser can do most of this with two open-source libraries and a <canvas> . Here's how the pieces fit together, with the code that matters and the limits we ran into. The building blocks pdf-lib edits the structure of a PDF: copy pages between documents, rotate them, read and write metadata, draw text and images. It doesn't render anything. PDF.js is Firefox's PDF renderer.
articles.author: Frank

articles.title: Your AI can give a wrong answer confidently. 🤖
articles.excerpt: And the problem might not even be the LLM. While working with a brand-focused AI application, Ive been learning why building reliable AI systems requires more than just writing a good prompt. Think ab…
articles.body: And the problem might not even be the LLM. While working with a brand-focused AI application, Ive been learning why building reliable AI systems requires more than just writing a good prompt. Think about a system that generates marketing copy using a brands knowledge base. Several things need to work together: → Brand context: Does the AI understand the brand, its audience, and its positioning? → Retrieval: Did the system find the right information from the uploaded documents? → Generation: Did the LLM use that information correctly? Heres what makes debugging interesting: If the system retrieves the wrong information, improving the prompt might not fix the problem.

articles.title: When Should You Stop Adding Features?
articles.excerpt: Introduction — The temptation to keep adding more When designing an application, ideas never seem to run out. A new option, an additional dashboard, an automation, an integration… Every idea seems cap…
articles.body: Introduction — The temptation to keep adding more When designing an application, ideas never seem to run out. A new option, an additional dashboard, an automation, an integration… Every idea seems capable of improving the product. So we add one feature. Then another. And another, until the application becomes harder to understand, use, and maintain. Yet one question deserves to be asked before every new addition: does this feature genuinely bring value to the user? 1. The trap of a product that tries to do everything An application can gradually drift away from its original purpose. By trying to meet every possible need, it accumulates options, screens, and rules. User journeys become longer. Choices multiply.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.title: 'We basically did Top Gun in space': 'Star Trek Starfleet Academy' warps back into action in March 2027 for sophomore year in the final frontier
articles.excerpt: The sophomore season of "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy" will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.
